reason: The cited evidence (E1) discusses interstitial effects on strength and ductility in other HEAs and mentions stacking faults, ε-martensite, and twins, but it does not provide data on SFE variation with temperature/strain rate in the Co-free alloy, nor does it demonstrate the proposed mechanism shift in that specific material. The key premises about SFE-mediated mechanism transitions in FeNiCrMn are therefore unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: SFE in FeNiCrMn decreases with temperature and increases with strain rate
Lower SFE promotes dissociation into partials, twinning, and martensite
Twinning/martensite increase work hardening and maintain ductility
Higher temperature/lower rate favor conventional dislocation slip
Co-free FeNiCrMn behaves analogously to CoCrFeMnNi in these mechanisms
